newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures firm, supported by weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures firm, supported by weak yen.

text.p: Yen-based gold futures ended firmer on Friday in lacklustre trade, reflecting the yen's weaker tendency against the dollar, traders said.
Prices ranged from one to four yen per gram firmer, with benchmark October finishing up four yen at 1,344 yen.
Static prices in gold futures limited the participation by private investors, although they rolled over long positions in the December contract to forward months, they said.
Trade houses were wary of engaging in arbitrage trade, as firmer short-term gold lease rates made trade houses wary of building fresh shorts in the spot market, they said.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $372.10/40 per ounce at the Tokyo close after gold fixed in London at $372.20 per ounce, the lowest since April 25.
In the continued bearish sentiment, spot gold was pressured by constant selling from overseas investors, including Australian producers.
"Investment funds are eyeing spot gold breaking under the support at $370 per ounce. After that, they could cover their short positions," one trader said,
Platinum futures ended mixed as investors liquidated their longs in nearbys, while made fresh buying in distant months.
Platinum futures ranged from five yen per gram lower to six yen firmer. Benchmark October was up six yen at 1,365 yen.
Spot platinum was a shade firmer at $374.75/375.50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, after opening at $374.00/374.75.
"Sentiment in platinum group metals remains bearish as talk that Russia was continuing to sell the metals despite low prices was cited as one bearish factor," one trader said.
Benchmark October palladium futures were up two yen at 422 yen. Benchmark October silver futures were down 0.4 yen per 10 grams at 175.7 yen.
